Full layouts of per CPU deferred, batch work, cache, node, barn, sheaf, slab, and info structures beyond referenced fields.
RCU grace, workqueue, monitor period, and flush worker selection semantics beyond shown waits.
Barn and sheaf sizing, allocation thresholds, and reclamation policy beyond shown emptying.
Sanitizer, fenced allocator, large allocation, and tracking interactions beyond shown hooks.

findings.text: Shrink entry for a cache first invokes sanitizer shrink hook then requests backend reclamation that flushes per CPU state and discards empty slabs, returning backend status.

Shutdown entry flushes per CPU state under CPU protection, waits for grace period when per CPU sheaf support is present, shrinks per node sheaf stores, then releases empty partial slabs and reports whether any slabs remain.
Sensitive free entry determines usable size, and when nonzero unpoisons and explicitly clears that span before releasing the allocation through the normal free path.

Size query validates the pointer including null and zero sized markers plus tag accessibility, prefers fenced allocation size when present, otherwise resolves large allocation size or owning slab size, returning zero on invalid input.

Diagnostic dump entry rejects low or non linear addresses and addresses without owning slab, otherwise gathers owning cache and object placement plus allocation history when retained and emits a summary with optional call stacks, returning success.

Per cache per CPU drain entries schedule a flush worker on each online CPU and wait for completion, with one variant always visiting every CPU for RCU sheaves and another skipping CPUs without used sheaf state.
Cache teardown helpers expose removal of kernel object linkage only when currently visible in sysfs and removal of debugfs entry only when debugfs root exists.
Global kmalloc description state comprises per type bucket pointers, init only size descriptor table, read only small size to index map, and a read only random seed influencing placement.

A per CPU deferred free context needs offload when any bulk queue holds entries or the linked head is set, while a batch slot is considered busy when any of its detached bulk queues holds entries or its detached head is set.

Both shutdown and shrink report absence of remaining slabs with zero and presence with one, with shutdown treating unreclaimed partial or node slabs as remaining and shrink treating any node with remaining slabs as remaining.

Size descriptors are ordered by internal index rather than numeric size, starting with zero then mid small sizes before ascending powers of two, and the small lookup maps successive eight byte steps to those indexes.

Slabinfo iteration acquires global cache list protection on start and releases on stop, walks the global cache list positionally, prints a version header before the first entry, and formats per cache occupancy plus tuning plus slab counts.
Detaching per CPU pending queues into a batch slot and scheduling its work executes under the per CPU context interrupt safe raw spin exclusion, with counters reset and queues exchanged while held.
Both per CPU flush variants require CPU hotplug read protection held by the caller and internally serialize with a global flush mutex across the schedule phase and the wait phase.

Barn sheaf lists and their counters are detached under barn interrupt safe spin exclusion with reclamation outside, node partial lists are mutated under node list spin exclusion with slab release outside, and debug object map construction is serialized by a dedicated spin lock.
Proc slabinfo list traversal holds the global slab list mutex for the whole sequence from open start through stop.

Per CPU deferred context carries per channel bulk queues and counts plus a linked head and count, an array of batch slots, and monitor delayed work; each batch slot carries per channel detached bulk queues, a detached head with grace snapshot, and RCU work item.

Object info result records queried pointer, owning slab, owning cache, aligned object start, adjustment for debug red zone, and when user tracking is enabled allocation return address plus bounded allocation and free stacks.
Per CPU sheaf usage is indicated by presence of spare or RCU pending sheaf or nonempty main sheaf, and per node barn tracks counts of full and empty sheaf lists alongside those lists.

Global deferred free barrier has an offload stage that ensures every per CPU pending queue is moved into scheduled batch work with waiting for in flight batches, followed by a drain stage that synchronously cancels monitor work and waits for all batch work completion.

A batch slot cycles among idle with all detached queues empty, attached with at least one detached queue populated and work scheduled, and reclaiming until work completion returns it to idle and makes it eligible for reuse.

Per node shrink triage moves fully free slabs to a discard set for release outside locking and reorders partially free slabs with fewest free objects toward the front, preserving the invariant that no fully occupied slab stays on the partial list.
Shutdown progresses from per CPU flush through optional grace wait and barn emptying to partial slab discard, ending in empty success or nonempty failure depending on remaining slabs.

Shrink reads occupancy as an upper bound because concurrent frees can proceed under list protection, RCU sheaf flush must tolerate a concurrent free removing the sheaf, and global barrier must tolerate concurrent producers adding new deferred objects.

Size and shutdown paths trap invalid states with warnings or fatal checks for missing slab association, full slabs on partial lists, interrupts disabled during partial free, malformed object placement, and leftover objects reported with offsets and tracking.
Slabinfo proc entry uses mode 0400 and announces format major two minor one, with columns for identity and occupancy and tuning and slab aggregates.

Size descriptors count twenty two entries from zero through two megabytes, comprising zero plus small set ninety six and one ninety two and eight through one twenty eight, then doubling from two fifty six upward with short labels using kilo and mega suffixes.

Small lookup holds twenty four entries for eight byte steps from eight to one ninety two, with index pattern three then four then two fives then four sixes then four ones then four sevens then eight twos.

Per size descriptors provide name families for normal plus optional reclaim and accounting and DMA and partition and no extension variants, using distinct prefixes for each family with size suffix, where disabled families expand to nothing and partition family expands cumulatively up to fifteen numbered members.
Slabinfo file operations bind sequence start next stop show handlers and proc operations bind open read seek release with permanent entry flag, created during init under the name slabinfo.
